events.text:
[IT Help chat · signed in as Brenda Walsh (E2901) · ticket T-6009]
hi, my phone says my work account is locked?? I keep getting an error when it tries to check my email. Can you unlock it for me please

args.summary: Account locked after 11 failed sign-ins today from Bucharest, RO (never previously signed in from there). A new MFA device (MD-2901-2, "Android device") was also registered at 08:02 today. Possible compromise. No unlock or other action taken.

args.note: Unlock requested. Account shows 11 failed sign-ins from RO (new country) and a new MFA device today. Escalated to Security; no account changes made.

events.text:
Brenda, I can't unlock your account right now. It was locked after repeated failed sign-in attempts today from Bucharest, Romania, and your account has no earlier sign-ins from there. That pattern can mean someone else is trying to get into it.

I've passed this to our Security on-call team (reference SEC-500), and they should contact you within about an hour. Until they do, I can't unlock the account, reset your password or change your MFA devices.

Please tell Security if you don't recognise the new authenticator device ("Android device") that was added to your account this morning at 8:02 AM.

Oh no, Bucharest? I've never been there, and I haven't been anywhere but Portland all week. I'm a bit worried now.

I don't know anything about an Android device being added, though. I only use my Pixel 8 for the authenticator, and I haven't added any new phone or device recently. I did get a couple of odd sign-in prompts on my phone this morning, and I tapped deny on both because I didn't start them.

Will Security reach me on my mobile? And is there anything I should do in the meantime, like changing my password?

args.note: Follow-up from employee: has never been in Romania, did not add the new "Android device" MFA device (MD-2901-2), and denied two unexpected sign-in prompts this morning. Escalated under SEC-500; no account changes made by the desk.

events.text:
Thanks, Brenda. That's useful, and I've added it to the ticket for Security: you've never been in Romania, you didn't add the Android device, and you denied two prompts you didn't start. Denying those prompts was the right call.

**Will Security reach you on your mobile?** I can't say which channel they'll use. They'll contact you directly, usually within an hour of the escalation. Keep an eye on your phone and your work chat.

**Should you change your password?** I'd wait for Security. I can't reset your password or change your MFA devices myself while this is open, because they need to review the account first. They'll tell you when and how to do it safely, including removing the device you didn't add.

**In the meantime:**
- Keep denying any sign-in prompt you didn't start. Never approve one, even if it seems to be from IT.
- Don't share any codes or passwords with anyone who contacts you, including someone claiming to be IT. We won't ask for them.
- If you use the same password on any other accounts, plan to change those soon.
- If you clicked a link or entered your password on an unfamiliar page recently, tell Security when they contact you.

Okay, thanks. I'll keep an eye on my phone and work chat. I haven't clicked any links or typed my password anywhere strange as far as I know, but I'll tell Security if I remember anything. I'm not using that password anywhere else, I don't think, so I'll leave it alone until they say.

Is there anything I can do on my desktop meanwhile, or should I just wait for their call?

Your account is locked, so anything that needs your work sign-in, such as email, chat on a new session or company apps, probably won't work until Security finishes. That also means you can't sign in on your desktop with your work account right now.

**What you can do:**
- Keep your phone and work chat close so you don't miss Security's contact.
- Do any work that doesn't need your work account, such as local files or paper tasks.
- Ask a colleague or your manager, Paul Lindgren, to cover anything urgent that depends on your email or systems.
- Don't try to sign in repeatedly. It won't unlock the account and may add more failed attempts to the log.

**What you shouldn't do:**
- Don't use a colleague's login or share your credentials to get around the lock.

Security's response time is about an hour. If you haven't heard from them by then, write back here and I'll follow up. Your ticket is T-6009.

Okay, thanks. I'll wait for their call and keep an eye on my phone. Ticket T-6009, got it.

Would you mind letting me know here if they don't reach me within the hour? I'm not sure what to do if nothing comes through.

I can't message you first. I only reply when you write to me in this chat, so I can't watch the clock and ping you if Security doesn't call.

If you haven't heard from them by about 11:00 AM, write back here or open a new chat and quote **T-6009** and **SEC-500**. I'll then check the ticket and chase it with Security. If you'd like a person to take over at that point, say so and I'll hand you to a desk lead.

Because your account is locked, you may not be able to sign in to this chat from your own account later. If so, you can reach us from the guest kiosk. We'd need to verify your identity again first. Quote the same two reference numbers.

Thanks for flagging this quickly, Brenda.

Oh, I see, so I have to come back to you. Okay, I'll write here by 11:00 if I haven't heard from Security, and I'll quote T-6009 and SEC-500.

Thanks for your help. I'll keep an eye on my phone.

You're welcome, Brenda. To recap: Security is working on SEC-500 and should contact you within about an hour. If you haven't heard anything by 11:00 AM, write back here with T-6009 and SEC-500. Take care until then.
